rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mirṣād is a place or boundary where watching and surveillance take place.
rows.anchor: المرصاد : الحد الذي يكون فيه الرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the limit and destination of the tyrants, where they are watched for punishment.
rows.anchor: أن جهنم هي حد الطاغين الذي يرصدون فيه للعذاب وهي مآبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that angels await the people of Paradise at Hell, which they cross, while it remains the tyrants’ destination.
rows.anchor: أو هي مرصاد لأهل الجنة ترصدهم الملائكة الذين يستقبلونهم عندها

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada likewise describe it as a route and passage for the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة نحوه ، قالا : طريقا وممرا لأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن يعمر
rows.claim: Ibn Yaʿmur reads the hamza of inna with fatḥa, making Hell’s being an ambush the reason for establishing the Hour and recompense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن يعمر ( أن جهنم ) بفتح الهمزة على تعليل قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both lābithīn and lubthīn are read; lābithīn is stronger because it suggests settled, habitual residence, unlike mere staying.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( لابثين ) ( ولبثين ) واللبث أقوى ، لأن اللابث من وجد منه اللبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥqāb means one epoch after another without end; the word is commonly used for successive periods, as its derivation suggests.
rows.anchor: حقبا بعد حقب ، كلما مضى حقب تبعه آخر إلى غير نهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported definition makes a ḥuqb eighty years.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحقب ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible interpretation has them remain for epochs without cold or drink except boiling water and ghassaq, then undergo another kind of punishment after those epochs.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : لابثين فيها أحقابا غير ذائقين فيها بردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative derives aḥqāb from drought or being deprived of provision, and construes it as a circumstantial description of their deprivation.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر : وهو أن يكون من ( حقب عامنا ) إذا قل مطره

words: لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explains their deprivation; the exception is disconnected: they have neither relief from the heat nor thirst-quenching drink, but taste boiling water and ghassaq.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء منقطع ، يعني : لا يذوقون فيها بردا وروحا ينفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported sense of al-bard is sleep, supported by a poetic line and the Arab saying that cold prevented sleep.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( البرد ) النوم ، وأنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghassāqan is read both with a light and a doubled sīn; it means what flows from the inhabitants’ pus.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( غساقا ) بالتخفيف والتشديد : وهو ما يغسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wifāqan is either a verbal noun used adjectivally or an ellipsis for something possessing correspondence.
rows.anchor: { وفاقا } وصف بالمصدر . أو ذا وفاق

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywah reads wifāqan on the fiʿāl pattern from waffaqahu, meaning that something was made to accord with another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة : ( وفاقا ) فعال من وفقه كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faʿʿāl pattern is common among eloquent Arabs for verbal nouns of faʿala verbs, as in kadhdhaba and kidhāban.
rows.anchor: وفعال في باب فعل كله فاش في كلام فصحاء من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab listener praised the author’s explanation with a play on the emphatic pattern, saying he had explained an āya with exceptional force.
rows.anchor: وسمعني بعضهم أفسر آية فقال لقد فسرتها فسارا ما سمع بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lightened reading, kidhāban, is treated as the verbal noun of kadhaba; its supporting poetic evidence continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتخفيف ، وهو مصدر كذب ، بدليل قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightened kidhāban is a verbal noun of kadhaba, supported by a poet’s line about affirming and denying; the verse’s form is compared with Noah 71:17.
rows.anchor: فصدقتها وكذبتها … والمرء ينفعه كذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kidhāban may be construed with kadhdhabū because that verb entails lying: whoever rejects the truth is a liar.
rows.anchor: لأن كل مكذب بالحق كاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If understood as mutual denial, the word describes reciprocal accusation: each side regards the other as liars.
rows.anchor: فمعناه : وكذبوا بآياتنا ، فكاذبوا مكاذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they spoke with extreme, competitive excess in lying, as though striving to outdo one another.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم يتكلمون بما هو إفراط في الكذب فعل من يغالب في أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kidhāban can be a plural of kādhib, or an intensive singular meaning an inveterate liar; in the latter sense it describes an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الكذاب بمعنى الواحد البليغ في الكذب

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammāl reads kullu shayʾin aḥṣaynāhu with kullu nominative as the start of a sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال : وكل شيء أحصيناه ، بالرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāban is a verbal noun functioning as an object in the sense of recording; aḥṣaynā means katabnā because reckoning and writing both imply precise preservation.
rows.anchor: مصدر في موضع إحصاء وأحصينا في معنى كتبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kitāban is circumstantial, meaning their deeds were written in the Preserved Tablet and in the recording angels’ scrolls.
rows.anchor: أو يكون حالا في معنى : مكتوبا في اللوح وفي صحف الحفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is an enumeration of their sins, as in the verse saying God counted them while they forgot; this is an aside.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { أحصاه الله ونسوه } ( المجادلة : 6 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste punishment follows from their disbelief in the reckoning and denial of the signs.
rows.anchor: مسبب عن كفرهم بالحساب وتكذيبهم بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is exceptionally severe: its wording makes any cessation of additional punishment seem almost impossible.
rows.anchor: على أن ترك الزيادة كالمحال الذي لا يدخل تحت الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in address is an instance of iltifāt and signals that the anger has reached its extreme.
rows.anchor: وبمجيئها على طريقة الالتفات شاهدا على أن الغضب قد تبالغ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says this is the most severe verse in the Qurʾān for the people of the Fire; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1263 ) ( هذه الآية أشد ما في القرآن على أهل النار )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a curse against the human being; it is among the harshest because killing is the ultimate worldly hardship and horror.
rows.anchor: دعاء عليه ، وهي من أشنع دعواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an exclamation at the excess of human ingratitude for God’s blessings, expressed with exceptional severity and compression.
rows.anchor: تعجب من إفراطه في كفران نعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage traces human life from its beginning, emphasizing abundant blessings and the person’s ingratitude, heedlessness, and failure to give thanks.
rows.anchor: من ابتداء حدوثه ، إلى أن انتهى وما هو مغمور فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: from what lowly, contemptible thing did God create him? Its answer follows in the next verse.
rows.anchor: من أي شيء حقير مهين خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human from a drop of fluid and then measured and prepared him for what suits and distinguishes him.
rows.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له ويختص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This measured creation recalls the statement that God created everything and determined it precisely.
rows.anchor: وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative by an elided yassara, which the following yassara explains.
rows.anchor: نصب السبيل بإضمار ( يسر ) وفسره بيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path may be the passage out of the mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: ثم سهل سبيله وهو مخرجه من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the path of good or evil a person chooses, made accessible through ability and empowerment.
rows.anchor: أو السبيل الذي يختار سلوكه من طريقي الخير والشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the path as God making clear the way of good and the way of evil.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بين له سبيل الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honored the human by giving him a grave for burial, rather than leaving him exposed as carrion for beasts and birds like other animals.
rows.anchor: فجعله ذا قبر يوارى فيه تكرمة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabara means to bury the dead; aqbara means to command or enable someone to bury him, as in the request made to al-Ḥajjāj about Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: وأقبره الميت . إذا أمره أن يقبره ومكنه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ansharahu means that God will bring the human into the next creation.
rows.anchor: أنشأه النشأة الأخرى . وقرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has nasharahu in place of ansharahu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( نشره ) { كلا } ردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the human for his present conduct.
rows.anchor: ردع للإنسان عما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lammā yaqḍ means he has not yet fulfilled God’s command, despite the long span from Adam to the present.
rows.anchor: لم يقض بعد ، مع تطاول الزمان وامتداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No human has ever been entirely free of shortcomings in carrying out all of God’s commands.
rows.anchor: يعني : أن إنسانا لم يخل من تقصير قط

words: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled lām in lammā, in is negative; with the lightened form, mā is extra and in is the lightened emphatic particle. Both readings suit the oath’s answer.
rows.anchor: لا تخلو فيمن قرأ لما مشددة

words: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause every soul has a guardian answers the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian is a watchful overseer, which the author identifies as God, citing descriptions of God as watchful and sustaining.
rows.anchor: مهيمن عليها رقيب ، وهو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the guardian as an angel who preserves each person’s deeds and counts the good and evil he earns.
rows.anchor: ملك يحفظ عملها ويحصى عليها ما تكسب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that 160 angels protect a believer like flies are driven from a bowl of honey; if left alone even briefly, devils would snatch him. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying every soul has a guardian, the text urges reflection on humanity’s first creation: the Creator can restore and recompense, so one should prepare for that day and give the guardian a pleasing record.
rows.anchor: أن على كل نفس حافظا ، أتبعه توصية الإنسان بالنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question from what was he created is answered by he was created from a spurting fluid.
rows.anchor: { مم خلق } استفهام جوابه { خلق من ماء دافق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāfiq may attribute the fluid to the act of pouring, like lābin and tāmir attribute things to their sources.
rows.anchor: النسبة إلى الدفق الذي هو مصدر دفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dāfiq is a figurative attribution: the pouring properly belongs to the fluid’s owner.
rows.anchor: والدفق في الحقيقة لصاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not say two fluids because they mingle in the womb and unite as human creation begins.
rows.anchor: لم يقل ماءين لامتزاجهما في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fluid emerges between the man’s backbone and the woman’s breastbones, where a necklace rests.
rows.anchor: من بين صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣulb is read with the two vowels fatḥa or ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( الصلب ) بفتحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word has four forms—ṣalb, ṣulb, ṣilib, and ṣālib; al-ʿAjjāj’s line uses ṣulb for a backbone compared to a leather-covered rein.
rows.anchor: في صلب مثل العنان المؤدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation assigns bone and sinew to the man, and flesh and blood to the woman.
rows.anchor: العظم والعصب من الرجل ، واللحم والدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in inna-hu refers to the Creator, indicated by the earlier mention of creation.
rows.anchor: الضمير للخالق ، لدلالة خلق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator who first made the human from a drop is plainly able to recreate him; doing so presents no difficulty or incapacity.
rows.anchor: على إعادته خصوصا { لقادر } لبين القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other construals take the return as return to the point of emergence from the loins, the urethra, or the original state; on these readings the day phrase takes an omitted governing verb.
rows.anchor: إلى مخرجه من الصلب والترائب أو الإحليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the primary reading of return as resurrection, yawm is governed by rajʿ; on the other interpretations it is governed by an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل الضمير في { رجعه } وفسره برجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innermost beliefs, intentions, and hidden deeds are exposed and examined, distinguishing what is good from what is corrupt.
rows.anchor: ما أسر في القلوب من العقائد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan heard a man recite a poem about concealed affection remaining within until secrets are exposed; Hasan said the man overlooked what Sūrat al-Ṭāriq says.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه سمع رجلا ينشد : سيبقى لها في مضمر القلب والحشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human will have no personal strength or defense by which to protect himself.
rows.anchor: فما للإنسان { من قوة } من منعة في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will have no helper or protector to ward harm away.
rows.anchor: ولا ناصر } ولا مانع يمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is revealed as ordered discourse, sent down in stages according to needs, opened with praise and ended with seeking refuge, and arranged into sūras and verses.
rows.anchor: أنزل القرآن كلاما مؤلفا منظما ونزله بحسب المصالح منجما وجعله بالتحميد مفتتحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is Arabic and free of crookedness; it speaks with clear proofs, opens religious and worldly benefits, and confirms earlier heavenly books.
rows.anchor: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج مفتاحا للمنافع الدينية والدنيوية مصداقا لما بين يديه من الكتب السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is a lasting miracle that defeats every rival across time, place, and language.
rows.anchor: عجزا باقيا دون كل معجز على وجه كل زمان دائرا من بين سائر الكتب على كل لسان في كل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eloquent Arabs could not produce anything equal to it, or even approach its shortest sūra; their failure despite intense opposition shows they knew its proof could not be answered.
rows.anchor: فلم يتصد للإتيان بما يوازيه أو يدانيه واحد من فصحائهم ولم ينهض لمقدار أقصر من سورة منه ناهض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents eventually answered the challenge with the sword alone, since they knew the Qurʾān’s argument had overwhelmed them.
rows.anchor: فلم يعارضوا الا السيف وحده على ان السيف القاضب مخراق لاعب إن لم تمض الحجة حده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes blessings on Muḥammad, describing him as God’s beloved, protected and supported by wisdom, unlettered, and named in the Torah and Gospel, along with his family, successors, Emigrants, and Helpers.
rows.anchor: والصلاة والسلام على خير من اوحى اليه حبيب الله أبي القاسم محمد بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In most sciences, scholars’ and craftspeople’s ranks are close, with only small differences in advancement.
rows.anchor: متن كل علم وعمود كل صناعة طبقات العلماء فيه متدانية وأقدام الصناع فيه متقاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest disparities arise in subtle insights, fine meanings, and hidden secrets that only the rarest specialists can uncover.
rows.anchor: ما في العلوم والصناعات من محاسن النكت والفقر ومن لطائف معان يدق فيها مباحث للفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr is the richest and most demanding science because its fine points overwhelm minds and its hidden meanings are difficult to reach; al-Jāḥiẓ makes this point in Naẓm al-Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: علم التفسير الذي لا يتم لتعاطيه وإجالة النظر فيه كل ذي علم كما ذكر الجاحظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expertise in law, theology, reports, preaching, grammar, or lexicon alone does not qualify one to interpret; the interpreter must excel in Qurʾānic semantics and eloquence and master other fields through study and review.
rows.anchor: لا يتصدى منهم أحد لسلوك تلك الطرائق ولا يغوص على شيء من تلك الحقائق الا رجل قد برع في علمين مختصين بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualified interpreter must have a precise, alert, flexible mind, command of prose and verse styles, and practice arranging and composing words.
rows.anchor: مسترسل الطبيعة منقادها مشتعل القريحة وقادها يقظان النفس دراكا للمحة وإن لطف شأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author shortened an earlier work while preserving many benefits and probing its hidden meanings; it was completed during Abū Bakr’s caliphate though he had expected the work to take over thirty years, and he credits the sanctuary’s blessing.
rows.anchor: فأخذت في طريقة أخصر من الأولى مع ضمان التكثير من الفوائد والفحص عن السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fātiḥa is Meccan, though another view says it is both Meccan and Medinan because it descended once in each city.
rows.anchor: مكية وقيل مكية ومدنية لأنها نزلت بمكة مرة وبالمدينة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called Umm al-Qurʾān because it contains the Qurʾān’s meanings: praise of God, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وتمسمى أم القرآن لاشتمالها على المعاني التي في القرآن من الثناء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also called Sūrat al-Kanz and al-Wāfiya because it encompasses those meanings.
rows.anchor: وسورة الكنز والوافية لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Ḥamd and al-Mathānī because it is repeated in every prayer unit.
rows.anchor: وسورة الحمد والمثاني لأنه تثني في كل ركعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Ṣalāh because reciting it in prayer makes the prayer excellent or sufficient.
rows.anchor: وسورة الصلاة لأنها تكون فاضلة أو مجزئة بقراءتها فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its other names include Sūrat al-Shifāʾ and al-Shāfiya.
rows.anchor: وسورة الشفاء والشافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has seven verses by agreement, though the excerpt breaks off while introducing a differing counting view.
rows.anchor: وهي سبع آيات بالاتفاق الا أن منهم من عد
